title: Deliver the next clean packaged evaluator and runtime product slice
description:
Outcome: Extend the proven Vibeformer pipeline beyond pkl-parser into the next coherent in-scope Pkl library slice covering evaluator/runtime and value-model behavior needed by normal .NET consumers, while retaining parser package behavior and the full product goal.

Architectural constraints: derive complete production inputs, generated sources, resources, and resolved compile classpaths from the actual upstream projects. Use live resolved Spoon frontend objects for Java and PSI plus the Kotlin Analysis API for Kotlin. Translate frontend objects directly and recursively through resolved type, executable, constructor, and field identities. Do not introduce a database, serialized fact model, second reconstructed AST, source-text parser, hand-edited generated C#, or product-specific semantics in the generic translator runtime.

Scope discipline: product-goal.md and port-scope.md remain authoritative. This epic is a bounded implementation milestone, not project completion, and it creates no exclusions for evaluator semantics, value model, module/resource loading, project/package settings, security policy, public library APIs, or C# code generation that remain outside its first selected dependency-closed slice.

Acceptance: record a dependency-closed upstream source and public API slice chosen from concrete evaluator/runtime call paths; resolve every included Java and Kotlin production input with zero unresolved/ambiguous/fallback symbols; translate reachable declarations and bodies with zero skipped/unsupported/fallback items; regenerate disposable C# cleanly; compile and pack with zero warnings/errors; consume only the package from an independent .NET project; and compare representative observable behavior with separately run authoritative upstream tests or an oracle. File dependencies and follow-ups for in-scope product work not required to complete this bounded slice without narrowing the product goal.

title: Deliver a clean packaged pkl-parser proof through direct Spoon translation
description:
## Outcome

Deliver the first architectural proof required by vibeformer/doc/architecture.md: translate the complete upstream pkl-parser production module directly from a resolved Spoon semantic model into disposable C#, compile it from scratch, pack it, consume it independently, and compare observable behavior with upstream Pkl.

## Current evidence and history

- Vibeformer is intentionally reset to deps.edn and durable docs; no src, test, generator, or package project currently exists.
- The removed implementation grew through 179 sample-, inferred-fact-, no-classpath-, and Datomic-oriented beads and roughly 29K lines before the direct-translation reset. Do not recreate that path.
- The prior cleared epic pkl-ygbtd stated the full parser goal but had no executable child graph.
- The pinned research/pkl gitlink is f7cac257ade5775c1dfc255f4fda2eacc296e9d0.
- pkl-parser has 50 production Java files plus org/pkl/parser/errorMessages.properties, totaling 9,023 production lines. Its main compile classpath is JSpecify 1.0.0. Five upstream Kotlin test files and the LanguageSnippetTests corpus provide independent behavior evidence.

## Architectural constraints

- Use Spoon with the real production source set, resources, generated inputs if any, and resolved Gradle compile classpath. Accepted generation must not use no-classpath mode.
- Walk live Spoon frontend objects directly and recursively. Do not serialize or reconstruct a second AST, add a database, or reparse Java source text.
- Select type, executable, constructor, and field mappings from resolved symbol identity, including overload and generic information.
- Account for every reachable production declaration and executable body. Unsupported or unresolved semantics are blocking diagnostics; never silently skip, stub, or name-guess.
- Generated C# is disposable and receives no manual patches. Fix resolution, recursive translation, symbol mappings, project emission, or an explicitly owned focused helper, then regenerate.
- Use ordinary .NET APIs where they preserve behavior. Keep Pkl parser behavior in the generated/product implementation, not a generic compatibility runtime.
- Kotlin remains governed by the full product goal; when production Kotlin translation is reached it must use PSI plus the Kotlin Analysis API. This Java architectural proof is not an exclusion or a claim of project completion.

## Success Criteria

- A clean checkout at the pinned gitlink has one reproducible path that regenerates all pkl-parser C# and project/package inputs without manual edits.
- The resolved-model and recursive-coverage gates report zero unresolved, ambiguous, fallback, skipped, unsupported, or public-stub items for all production inputs.
- Fresh generated output builds and packs with compiler diagnostics mapped back to Spoon elements and translation/mapping rules.
- An independent .NET consumer, outside the generated solution, restores the produced NuGet package and exercises public lexer, parser, span, syntax-model, and error surfaces.
- A separately run upstream JVM oracle and the independent package consumer agree on representative upstream valid and invalid corpus behavior, including tokens, syntax structure, spans, and diagnostics where observable.
- Exact clean-generation, test, build, pack, consume, and differential commands and results are recorded on the beads that close them.
- Closing this epic proves only the first architectural module milestone; vibeformer/doc/product-goal.md remains the exclusive project-completion rule.

title: Preserve Java structural equality and hash semantics in packaged parser
description:
Outcome: Fix the resolved Objects.equals, Objects.deepEquals, and Objects.hash mappings so public generated parser syntax values preserve the Java structural equality and compatible hash contracts for collections, arrays, strings, enums, spans, and nested syntax nodes.

Review evidence: the upstream JVM at f7cac257ade5775c1dfc255f4fda2eacc296e9d0 parses two independent copies of name = 42 into GenericParser nodes with equals=true and identical hashCode values. The independently restored Pkl.Parser 0.0.0-development package parses the same source into nodes with Equals=false and different GetHashCode values. Generated Syntax/Generic/Node.cs routes children equality through JavaCompat.Equals, while runtime/Vibeformer.JavaCompat.cs delegates that operation to object.Equals and computes hashes from destination GetHashCode values. The existing 956-case differential gate compares parse observations but does not exercise public equality/hash behavior.

Requirements: correct the reusable resolved-symbol mapping or focused reviewable compatibility helper, regenerate without output patches, and add independent upstream/package observations for equal and unequal nested generic and typed syntax trees, list/array equality, and equality-hash consistency. Preserve fail-closed direct Spoon translation and do not add a reconstructed AST or database.

Acceptance: two separately parsed equivalent modules compare equal on both JVM and package sides and produce equal hashes within each runtime; meaningfully different trees compare unequal; nested list/array-backed public syntax values match upstream equality behavior; clean tests, generation, zero-warning compilation, packing, isolated consumption, and the expanded upstream differential gate all pass.
close_reason: Implemented reusable Java list structural equality/hash and recursive Objects.deepEquals array semantics; added independent package consumer and upstream/package observations for equal/unequal generic and typed trees, nested lists/arrays, and equality-hash consistency. Clojure tests, clean zero-warning generation/compilation, isolated NuGet consumption, and 956-case differential gate pass.
